# N12 current native source port

Source preparation only. The shared retention correction has12 portable data/
real-file tests passing; no .NET, compiler, native procedure, CI action or Git
mutation was executed. Ordinary product qualification remains closed.

## Entry and prerequisites

`adapter.execute(context, *, deadline)` uses the same13-key root context as the
[owner-death bridge](../owner-death/README.md#entry-contract). It adopts the shared
dispatcher's existing root-owned0700 output containing exactly the five root600
plan/source/build/inventory/execution inputs, checks bindings and creates all new
leaves exclusively. It returns one exact case row for **N12 only**.

The full current capture and actual CLI/helper locked-restore/Release-publication
logs/maps are verified with [binding.py](../../binding.py). The genuine peer helper
comes from the current receipt's helpers.peer.image and is retained through
[slot/helpers.py](../slot/helpers.py). Both historical N02 and N03 prerequisites
still execute physically; they receive no duplicate case credit.

The shared [bridge](../n11/bridge.py) stages full actual inputs via the frozen
owner-death copy helpers with source_sealed=False. Source stays0700 directories/
0644-or0755 files; tool/runtime/helpers are0555 directories/0444-or0555 files. The
runtime is an actual compact FDD deployment, never a fake inventory of an SDK.
The original family shell creates its own request/workspace.

The real [OS audit](../os_audit.py) is called on one capped absolute deadline:
Audit(end), initialize_tools(), then build(runtime,tool,False,peer). The original
[runner](../native_process.py), literal dispatch/FIFO EOF joins, native shell and
retention collector preserve original root-unit/process ownership and cleanup.
No old build schema, TRX, source-review Boolean or successful native result is
fabricated. The N02 actor derives from the actual current checkout UID/GID and
is checked against real NSS; the root adapter cannot substitute a protected owner.

## Native behavior and clocks

N12 is the real leader exit with TERM-resistant descendant, original group stop, EOF joins and final actual RootCustody/account closure.

Fixture600/cleanup30 remain unchanged. The owner RuntimeMaxSec remains240 and TimeoutStopSec5. The historical request UTC derives once from remaining fixture time minus1; the original request>245-second prelaunch guard is preserved. Forcing a240-second request would mask this original guard.
The earlier outer absolute deadline remains in force; no native retry or renewed
allowance is introduced. A fixture failure stays failed even if retention succeeds.

## Evidence and reconciliation

`validate_evidence(context,evidence_raw,*,capture_raw)` checks only the bounded
current-source envelope. It establishes no physical fact. The mandatory
`verify_retained_evidence(context,*,deadline)` rereads actual retained leaves,
command metadata and logs and repeats all original readable record predicates
in [records.py](records.py). Run and aggregate must require both exact rows equal;
execute also performs retained reconciliation itself before returning.

N12-evidence.json binds the original USTAR digest and every unchanged
raw member. The actual collector writes control/native.tar; its stdout is only a
terminal marker. The adapter reads the actual bounded archive, validates it without
filesystem extraction, retains native-private.tar byte-exact, and retains each fixed
leaf individually. Aggregate rereads the original archive and all leaves; no archive
is reconstructed to manufacture its digest or record-validator input. Original8MiB
member/32MiB payload bounds remain, with a separate33,619,968-byte archive bound.
Each command requires exactly two typed stream rows and actual reads of both files,
including empty streams. See the [shared retention API and pitfalls](../n11/README.md#retention-helpers-and-pitfalls)
and [portable data/file controls](../../test_n11.py). Raw records are not echoed; no coverage or
counter arithmetic is performed. The N12 adapter imports the fixed N11 bridge
read-only, bound by the complete current capture.

## Metadata sampling without repeated subprocesses

The actual [N12 shell](checkpoint-n12-data-integration.sh) and
[None shell](../slot/checkpoint-none.sh) use the same `pin_file(path, hash,
byte_limit)` and `ancestor(path)` functions. `pin_file` parses size and link count
from its existing complete before sample (`device:inode:size:hex-mode:links:uid:gid`)
instead of starting separate `stat` commands for those two fields. It requires
exactly seven typed fields, the same byte cap and one link, the actual SHA256,
and the same complete after sample. `ancestor` reads UID and octal permissions
together for each component, preserving the actual lexical/symlink checks,
complete walk through `/`, root UID and nonwritable-mode predicate.

`alias_walk(record)` also reads the UID and octal mode of each ordinary path
component together. Its two complete walks still surround the resolved file
hash and full identity samples. Every symlink keeps its separate metadata,
target and second metadata checks; malformed fields, a nonroot UID, a writable
mode, changed link identity or an expired deadline still rejects.

These changes reduce subprocess calls, not verification checkpoints. There is no
cached physical result, skipped tree/OS check, renewed deadline, enlarged allowance
or changed prelaunch remainder guard. The
[metadata sample controls](../../test_metadata_sample_batching.py) execute the
actual Bash functions on ordinary temporary paths with controlled command data
and recorded calls. They establish parser/orchestration behavior only; no native
acceptance or actual time saving is claimed. Fresh bounded Linux execution remains
required to show that setup fits the original fixture budget.
